ploidyspec report: lpTriTurg1

Summary

Structure in this individual's assembly, read from the sections below; not inheritance and not origin. See docs/guide, Chapter 6.

Ploidy

2 haplotype copies of each of 14 chromosome numbers; the numbers form sets of 2 (7 homeolog pairs covering 100% of numbers), so x ≈ 7 and up to 4x relative to x; the sets are nearly as diverged as unrelated chromosomes, so they may be an old (paleo) duplication.

Confidence: high. Evidence: copies from the assembly (2 per number); 7 homeolog pairs covering 100% of numbers; homeolog distance 0.081 vs unrelated 0.081

Auto-like or allo-like?

Allo-like (disomic-like): the duplicated sets do not interchange, from homeolog pairs (pair-depth CV 0.01). This is also what a long-rediploidized autopolyploid looks like. The chromosome numbers form two subgenomes (7 and 7 numbers, size-independent z = 179) and every homeolog pair crosses them. Non-homologous chromosomes within a subgenome are closer (0.069) than homeologs across them (0.081): each subgenome carries its own repeats, as when two diverged genomes merge.

Confidence: high. Evidence: 14 chromosome numbers assessed: 14 split into lineages, 0 tetrasomic-like, 0 one divergent copy, 0 candidate; subgenomes chr01,chr02,chr07,chr08,chr09,chr11,chr12 | chr03,chr04,chr05,chr06,chr10,chr13,chr14 (z = 178.8); homeolog pairs tested across them

TE markers

Only the absolute marker fraction is available (two copies per number); it does not separate diploid, auto- and allopolyploid, so no reading is made from it.

Confidence: not assessable. Evidence: te_marker_fraction mean 0.0137

Rediploidization

Diverged throughout the paired chromosomes: no stretch where homeologs are as close as alleles. Rediploidization is complete, or the genome was allo-like from the start.

Confidence: medium. Evidence: residual tetrasomy on 0/14 homeolog-paired chromosome numbers; pair-depth CV 0.01; homeology map: 0% of the genome in 0 homeolog blocks, 0 chromosome pairs

Copy number and copy divergence (whole-chromosome matrix)

Hierarchically reordered, chromosome-number resolution

Same distance data as the heatmaps above, but collapsed to one value per chromosome NUMBER (haplotype copies aggregated away) and reordered by average-linkage clustering -- shows cross-chromosome (subgenome/ancestral-pair) structure cleanly, including diffuse structure with no individually FDR-significant pair. Red outlines mark individually FDR-accepted pairs from the homeolog test below. See INTERPRETATION.md's "checkerboard" section.
